title: I Kept the Confession About the Extra Scholarship Letter

parts.text: I mailed a second recommendation I was not supposed to send, and it worked. I am forty-one, teacher, still not proud. Luis needed a backup school after a portal glitch ate his first app. The counselor, Dana, had a cap: one rec per teacher per cycle. I wrote a second anyway, on my home printer that jams on cheap paper. The jam still has a triangle of letterhead I keep in a drawer. Luis got in. Dana later asked why the backup had my letter. I told her. She was angry, then tired, then asked me to write the cap exception for next year so nobody has to sneak. I did. This is morally grey and I live with it. The printer still jams. Luis sent a photo of a cafeteria name tag with no ranch this time. I did not tell the family chat. Some confessions are just policy waiting to be less stupid. I still think about the cap when I sign things. Dana said, "Did you send a second" I said, "Yes. The portal ate the first" Dana said don't make a habit. I said make an exception form. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened.

social.video_title: I broke the one-letter cap and then wrote the exception
social.description: A jammed printer triangle lives in my drawer. The student got in. Would you have waited for the cap?
